title: The Basis a Withdrawal's Release Is Measured On
content:
How many appraisals stand on a Keyturn Host Protection Plan enrolment in the recent period, and whether money stands booked as owed to the host, settle the basis a withdrawal's release is measured on.

- Where two or more appraisals stand on the enrolment in the two months before and money stands booked as owed to the host, the release is measured as that money less the largest appraisal standing, the loss being settled once under the appraisal that values it in full.
- Where exactly one appraisal stands in that period and money stands booked as owed, the release is measured as the money that appraisal booked.
- In every other case the release is measured as the whole of the money standing booked as owed.

### Figures worked through (hypothetical)

Suppose 5000 stands booked as owed on the enrolment, the largest appraisal standing on it valued 3000, and the most recent appraisal booked 1800.

| Appraisals in the two months before | Money standing booked as owed | Release measured at |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | 5000 | 2000.00 |
| 1 | 5000 | 1800.00 |
| 2 | nothing | nothing |
| none | 5000 | 5000.00 |

The largest appraisal standing is the largest at any time on the enrolment, not merely the largest inside the two months; where no money stands booked as owed, the last reading governs whatever the number of appraisals.

### What the records show

The appraisals counted are those standing on this enrolment within the two months before the withdrawal.
